answers.core: It fundamentally alters the `Script`/`GDScript` resources and adds a `Class` resource. I might poke around the C++ API to see if this is possible as a plugin/extension.
answers.workaround: From a user perspective, one can simply just avoid using the tag that starts a new file definition. For attaching scripts to nodes, this gets more complicated, but maybe a separate dialogue to select which class in the script you want to attach or the ability to select a class resource file instead of a script? Regardless, it would be more of a back-end change rather than an end-user change
